answer.headline: ATL leads the South Atlantic demand_only expansion screen, and its average departure delay has a positive calculated monthly slope
answer.body:
This is a screening rank of expansion opportunity for the Census South Atlantic division under the demand_only scenario, not a financial valuation.
Calculated demand_only scores, highest first, are ATL {F378}, MCO {F379}, MIA {F380}, CLT {F381}, FLL {F382}, IAD {F383}, TPA {F384}, BWI {F385}, RDU {F386}, DCA {F387}, RSW {F388}, DJT {F389}, CHS {F390}, JAX {F391}, SAV {F392}, RIC {F393}, ORF {F394}, SFB {F395}, MYR {F396}, GSP {F397}, PNS {F398}, VPS {F399}, PIE {F400}, SRQ {F401}, PGD {F402}, ILM {F403}, ECP {F404}, AVL {F405}, GSO {F406}, CAE {F407}, and EYW {F408}.
Tie flags compare each score only with the previous score and do not mean the scores are equal: MCO {F379} is not tied with ATL {F378}, MIA {F380} is tied with MCO {F379}, CLT {F381} is tied with MIA {F380}, FLL {F382} is not tied with CLT {F381}, IAD {F383} is not tied with FLL {F382}, TPA {F384} is not tied with IAD {F383}, BWI {F385} is tied with TPA {F384}, RDU {F386} is tied with BWI {F385}, DCA {F387} is not tied with RDU {F386}, RSW {F388} is tied with DCA {F387}, DJT {F389} is not tied with RSW {F388}, CHS {F390} is tied with DJT {F389}, JAX {F391} is tied with CHS {F390}, SAV {F392} is not tied with JAX {F391}, RIC {F393} is tied with SAV {F392}, ORF {F394} is tied with RIC {F393}, SFB {F395} is tied with ORF {F394}, MYR {F396} is tied with SFB {F395}, GSP {F397} is tied with MYR {F396}, PNS {F398} is tied with GSP {F397}, VPS {F399} is tied with PNS {F398}, PIE {F400} is tied with VPS {F399}, SRQ {F401} is tied with PIE {F400}, PGD {F402} is tied with SRQ {F401}, ILM {F403} is tied with PGD {F402}, ECP {F404} is tied with ILM {F403}, AVL {F405} is tied with ECP {F404}, GSO {F406} is tied with AVL {F405}, CAE {F407} is tied with GSO {F406}, and EYW {F408} is tied with CAE {F407}.
Every scored airport is flagged AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN because no verified FAA capacity rate is on file, so an airfield constraint is not established.
CARRIER_CONCENTRATION is also flagged for ATL at largest-carrier seat share {F285}, for MIA at {F301}, for CLT at {F290}, for IAD at {F297}, for BWI at {F287}, for SFB at {F312}, for PIE at {F306}, and for PGD at {F305}. The flag note says a hub tenant anchors leases but adds de-hubbing risk. That risk is not a measured outcome.
For ATL, the calculated demand_only score is {F378}. The score definition is {F378.definition}. The projected passenger-increase input is {F100}, realized passenger growth is {F193}, and home-CBSA per-capita income is {F254}. The passenger-increase input is an unconstrained FAA forecast. Realized growth and income are calculated inputs. The score itself is calculated.
In the other scenario columns returned with this screen, ATL is not ordered first. MIA is ordered first under base, EYW under equal_weights, and ILM under momentum_heavy.
Airports below the enplanement gate were not scored. TLH, with observed enplanements {F63}, is the first airport the screen lists below that gate. Airports in the division with no FAA enplanement record were also not scored.
Because ATL is the highest demand_only score and is not tied with MCO, the delay trend is for Hartsfield Jackson Atlanta International (ATL). Monthly departure delay here is average departure delay minutes. The ATL window is {F421.period}. Calculated monthly values are {F409.label} {F409}, {F410.label} {F410}, {F411.label} {F411}, {F412.label} {F412}, {F413.label} {F413}, {F414.label} {F414}, {F415.label} {F415}, {F416.label} {F416}, {F417.label} {F417}, {F418.label} {F418}, {F419.label} {F419}, and {F420.label} {F420}.
The calculated linear trend at ATL is {F421}. The calculated difference of the ending month minus the starting month is {F422}. Both are calculated. The slope caveat is that monthly series include seasonality and the slope is descriptive.
The screen and the delay series do not measure terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, or profitability.

The positive slope at ATL and the higher ending month describe a fitted line through a seasonal monthly series. That pattern does not establish a cause of delay, a steady operational deterioration, or an airfield or terminal constraint.
The hub-tenant note on CARRIER_CONCENTRATION does not establish that de-hubbing will occur, and neither the screen nor the delay series establishes unmet demand or a profitable expansion case.

assumptions: South Atlantic is the Census division of that name. The entity resolver returned that division as an exact group.
demand_only is the named screening scenario. The model enplanement gate was left unchanged.
The highest score is ATL. MCO is not flagged as tied with ATL, so the delay trend is for ATL alone. ATL is Hartsfield Jackson Atlanta International in Atlanta, GA.
Monthly departure delays means the catalog metric average departure delay minutes over the on-time months in the trend, rather than the departure delay rate.
limitations: The screen ranks expansion opportunity. It is not a valuation. Costs, debt, airline-agreement economics, and construction risk are not modelled.
The passenger-increase component is an unconstrained FAA forecast. It is not observed traffic and it is not unmet demand.
Terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured by these series.
Every scored airport is flagged AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN, so a verified airfield capacity constraint is not established.
Average departure delay covers domestic flights of reporting carriers only. International flights and non-reporting carriers are outside the series. Early departures do not reduce the delay total.
The monthly slope includes seasonality and is descriptive.
Airports below the enplanement gate, and airports with no FAA enplanement record, were not scored. Leaving them out is not a low rank.
A tie flag compares only the previous score. A chain of flags is not a mutual tie, and a flag does not mean the scores are equal.
The order is specific to demand_only weights. The other scenario columns in the same screen order different airports first.
